title: Biodiversity and Non-Timber Forest Products in the Tropical Forests in Tanah Papua, Indonesia
content: Although Papua (the western half of New Guinea) is world-renowned for its unparalleled biological diversity, floristic research, and the characterization of non-timber forest products (NTFPs), these areas have historically been poorly documented and understood compared to other tropical regions. This research analyzed species richness, diversity, and community structure of Arfak (201,757 ha) and Tambrauw (536,983 ha) forest management units (FMUs). Using stratified random sampling combined with the Whittaker Modified Plot (WMP) method, vegetation samples were collected from May 2024 to May 2025. Species richness, diversity, dominance, and dissimilarity were analyzed using the Vegan Package (R Core Team, 2016) in R (version 3.4.2). Species accumulation curves, rarefaction, and Jackknife estimators were used to improve the accuracy of species richness estimates, with 1000 replicates performed following standard practices. Non-timber forest product potential was then estimated according to species community composition and abundance patterns.
